body.estimand_functional: \(\theta\in[L(o,e),U(o,e)]\), with \(L=\max\{0,\sum_j a_j-k+1,\max_i(b_i-\sum_{j\neq i}h_j)\}\) and \(U=\min\{g,\min_j a_j,\min_{|S|\geq2}\sum_{j\in S}c_j/(|S|-1)\}\)

sampling_model.design: One observational block and one block for each single-treatment intervention; each block is multinomial on its stated finite alphabet.
sampling_model.units: The observational block has \(n_0\) independent common-population units and intervention block \(j\) has \(n_j\) independent common-population units; cross-block independence is not required for the union-bound coverage statement.
sampling_model.treatment: The observational treatment is factual, while block \(j\) records outcomes under the intervention \(X\leftarrow j\).
sampling_model.overlap: No positive-cell condition is imposed; zero observational and intervention cells are allowed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance functions are estimated; empirical multinomial cell frequencies enter the confidence polytope.

body.tldr: Common-population observational and single-treatment intervention margins determine the exact identified interval for any finite-alphabet scalar conjunction probability of causation. The published Shu--Wang--Li endpoints are attained for every compatible real input: an information-preserving indicator coarsening lifts back to all categorical cells, intersection packing attains the upper endpoint, and a deleted-diagonal maximum flow with a residual-failure invariant attains the lower endpoint. Rational inputs admit sorted endpoint evaluation, sparse exact SCM witnesses, and short active-affine or minimum-cut certificates; block-multinomial confidence-region inversion adds uniform finite-sample coverage without appropriating the directional asymptotics of Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li.

project_justification.gap: Shu--Wang--Li prove all-dimensional validity but leave pointwise tightness open, while Xie--Li's constructive proof is binary and generic response-signature programs conceal the scalar geometry in exponentially many response states.
project_justification.niche: The common-population scalar conjunction problem has a coupling structure in which factual failures delete diagonal edges and all unused row capacity can be filled inside a saturated failure union.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the exact indicator lifting, the packing and flow endpoint laws, the min-cut and sorted duals, audited polynomial witness complexity, and a boundary-safe finite-sample inversion of the resulting sharp interval.

body.related_work: Shu--Wang--Li Theorem 2 supplies the scalar affine formulas and explicitly leaves their general-dimensional tightness unresolved. Xie--Li Theorem 3.2 supplies the closest constructive precedent by solving the binary eight-cell system. Koperberg Proposition 6 supplies the finite Hall--Strassen coupling principle adapted to the lower deleted-diagonal network. Tian--Pearl supplies the binary PNS interval used solely as an unnumbered algebraic sanity regression for the general formulas and witness constructions. Li--Pearl provides the earlier recursive multivalued bounds but is not treated as a direct theorem target. Rossetto--Antonucci gives a generic sharp response-signature linear program and SCM realization; it is the computational baseline, not a theorem claimed to be improved in general. Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li gives the active-set directional limit theory, which is credited rather than relabeled. Horowitz--Lee, Stoye, and Kaido--Molinari--Stoye motivate confidence-region and projection inference, while the stated finite-sample result is specialized to the present block-multinomial polytope. Harinen and coauthors provide the hypothetical common-population customer-journey setting in which a prespecified multichannel response-pattern probability is a concrete scalar consumer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Scalar sharpness does not imply simultaneous sharpness for several response patterns. Separately summing scalar endpoint values can therefore produce an unattainable policy utility. The confidence interval is a conservative outer inversion and carries no optimal-width claim. The support bound \(N_\star\) is polynomial but is not asserted to equal the exact frontier \(s_\star(m,r,k)\), which compares the two separately minimized endpoint supports.
body.honest_scope: The finite max-flow/min-cut theorem, multinomial concentration, and polynomial-time rational linear programming are standard inputs. The all-alphabet TAKE refinement, endpoint constructions, residual invariant, support and denominator audit, and interval equality remain to be proved. Unequal alphabets and repeated queried labels are covered, but factual-conditioned representative PoCs, incomplete subpopulations, mediator restrictions, population mismatch, and simultaneous vectors of conjunctions are outside the theorem. The Tian--Pearl binary reduction is an unnumbered sanity corollary and regression test, not a research-target theorem; the proof plan retains its algebraic verification by specializing the endpoint formulas and both witness constructions to the binary case. For \(k=1\), the target is the known marginal \(a_1\); for \(r=1\), the interval is \([1,1]\). The exact order of \(s_\star(m,r,k)\), defined through the separate lower- and upper-endpoint minima over \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\), remains open.
